notes: προέφθασεν keeps 'spake first to' whole: 'first' realizes the preverb προ-, and the 'to' is the verb's own government of an accusative object, which has no case for an English preposition to realize (rule 106). Head on the verb word, never the particle; heading on 'first' is the competing reading and is refused by rule 106's head clause.
τῆς takes 'of the' headed on 'the' (rule 21) while γῆς stands alone; τῶν before υἱῶν is emptied by αὐτῶν (rule 20) and τῶν before ἀλλοτρίων is unrepresented, the ASV writing no determiner (rule 23).
ἐλθόντα keeps the supplied 'when' and the supplied subject 'he', the Greek expressing neither (rules 74, 86).
